::: {#exr-prac-score-zero}
#### Score at the MLE (adapted from @dobson4e, Chapter 3)

Let $\dsn{X} \siid \Pois(\rate)$.

**(a)** Write the log-likelihood $\llik(\rate; \vx)$.

**(b)** Derive the score function $\score(\rate; \vx)$.

**(c)** Find the MLE $\hat\rate_{ML}$,
and evaluate the score at the MLE.

**(d)** Provide an intuitive interpretation
of the value of the score at $\hat\rate_{ML}$.
:::

:::{#sol-prac-score-zero}

**(a)**

$$
\ba
\llik(\rate; \vx)
&= \logf{\prodin \frac{\rate^{\rvar_\iobs} e^{-\rate}}{\rvar_\iobs!}}
&& \text{(log of the likelihood of an $\iid$ sample)}
\\
&= \sumin \logf{\frac{\rate^{\rvar_\iobs} e^{-\rate}}{\rvar_\iobs!}}
&& \text{(log of a product)}
\\
&= \sumin \paren{\logf{\rate^{\rvar_\iobs} e^{-\rate}} - \logf{\rvar_\iobs!}}
&& \text{(log of a quotient)}
\\
&= \sumin \paren{\logf{\rate^{\rvar_\iobs}} + \logf{e^{-\rate}} - \logf{\rvar_\iobs!}}
&& \text{(log of a product)}
\\
&= \sumin \paren{\rvar_\iobs \logf{\rate} + \logf{e^{-\rate}} - \logf{\rvar_\iobs!}}
&& \text{(log of a power)}
\\
&= \sumin \paren{\rvar_\iobs \logf{\rate} - \rate - \logf{\rvar_\iobs!}}
&& \text{($\logt$ undoes $\expt$)}
\\
&= \sumin \rvar_\iobs \logf{\rate} - \sumin \rate - \sumin \logf{\rvar_\iobs!}
&& \text{(split the sum)}
\\
&= \paren{\sumin \rvar_\iobs}\logf{\rate} - \sumin \rate - \sumin \logf{\rvar_\iobs!}
&& \text{(factor $\logf{\rate}$ out of the first sum)}
\\
&= \paren{\sumin \rvar_\iobs}\logf{\rate} - n\rate - \sumin \logf{\rvar_\iobs!}
&& \text{(sum of $n$ copies of $\rate$)}
\ea
$$

**(b)**

$$
\ba
\score(\rate; \vx)
&= \deriv{\rate}\sb{\paren{\sumin \rvar_\iobs}\logf{\rate} - n\rate - \sumin \logf{\rvar_\iobs!}}
&& \text{(log-likelihood from (a))}
\\
&= \deriv{\rate}\sb{\paren{\sumin \rvar_\iobs}\logf{\rate}} - \deriv{\rate}\sb{n\rate}
   - \deriv{\rate}\sb{\sumin \logf{\rvar_\iobs!}}
&& \text{(linearity of differentiation)}
\\
&= \deriv{\rate}\sb{\paren{\sumin \rvar_\iobs}\logf{\rate}} - \deriv{\rate}\sb{n\rate} - 0
&& \text{(derivative of a constant)}
\\
&= \deriv{\rate}\sb{\paren{\sumin \rvar_\iobs}\logf{\rate}} - \deriv{\rate}\sb{n\rate}
&& \text{(drop the zero term)}
\\
&= \paren{\sumin \rvar_\iobs}\deriv{\rate}\logf{\rate} - n\deriv{\rate}\rate
&& \text{(constant multiple rule)}
\\
&= \paren{\sumin \rvar_\iobs}\rate^{-1} - n\deriv{\rate}\rate
&& \text{(derivative of $\log$)}
\\
&= \paren{\sumin \rvar_\iobs}\rate^{-1} - n
&& \text{(derivative of $\rate$ with respect to itself)}
\\
&= \frac{\sumin \rvar_\iobs}{\rate} - n
&& \text{(write the negative power as a fraction)}
\\
&= \frac{n\rvarbar}{\rate} - n
&& \text{($\textstyle\sumin \rvar_\iobs = n\rvarbar$)}
\ea
$$

**(c)**

The MLE solves $\score(\rate; \vx) = 0$,
so evaluating the score there afterwards is a check on the algebra.
Setting $\score(\rate; \vx) = 0$:

$$
\ba
0 &= \frac{n\rvarbar}{\rate} - n
&& \text{(score from (b))}
\\
\frac{n\rvarbar}{\rate} &= n
&& \text{(add $n$ to both sides)}
\\
n\rvarbar &= n\rate
&& \text{(multiply both sides by $\rate$)}
\\
\hat\rate_{ML} &= \rvarbar
&& \text{(divide both sides by $n$)}
\ea
$$

If $\rvarbar > 0$
(equivalently,
at least one $\rvar_\iobs > 0$),
then

$$
\ba
\score(\rvarbar; \vx)
&= \frac{n\rvarbar}{\rvarbar} - n
&& \text{(score from (b) at $\rate = \rvarbar$)}
\\
&= n - n
&& \text{(cancel $\rvarbar$, since $\rvarbar > 0$)}
\\
&= 0
&& \text{(subtract)}
\ea
$$

If instead all $\rvar_\iobs = 0$,
then $\rvarbar = 0$ and $\hat\rate_{ML} = 0$ is a boundary value.
In that case,
the score formula
$\score(\rate; \vx) = \frac{n\rvarbar}{\rate} - n$
is not defined at $\rate = 0$,
so the usual interior verification
$\score(\hat\rate_{ML}; \vx) = 0$
does not apply.

**(d)**

The score measures the rate of change of the log-likelihood.
When it equals zero,
increasing or decreasing $\rate$ slightly would not improve the fit;
we are at a "flat" point.
Intuitively,
$\hat\rate_{ML} = \rvarbar$ is the value of $\rate$ that makes
the expected count per observation ($\rate$) exactly equal to
the observed sample average count ($\rvarbar$).

:::
